incidents.vector: Phishing email gained access to Microsoft 365 mailboxes; firm lacked multi-factor authentication.
incidents.impact: Intruders read attorney email accounts for nearly a year (July 2024-June 2025), exfiltrating client names, financial accounts, medical data, and Social Security numbers. A proposed class action was filed May 26 alleging negligence; one plaintiff cites 19 fraudulent charges following the breach.

incidents.victim: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
incidents.vector: Intrusion attributed to an Iran-linked front group; entry vector not publicly disclosed.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole at least 700 GB of email, backups, and operational files, wiped data, and forced LACMTA to take parts of its network offline in March. Israeli researchers (Gambit Security) discovered exfiltrated data exposed online and confirmed Iranian state ties on May 26.

incidents.victim: Lithuania — Centre of Registers (state property/legal entity registry)
incidents.vector: Attackers misused legitimate login credentials issued to institutions authorized to query the registry, accessing data from a foreign country.
incidents.impact: More than 600,000 records exposed, including names, dates of birth, national ID numbers, addresses, and property/cadastral data. The Centre of Registers chief resigned; opposition politicians publicly alleged a Russian intelligence operation, citing risks of surveillance and targeting of officials.

incidents.victim: US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor created a public GitHub profile ("Private-CISA"), disabled built-in secret-scanning protections, and committed plaintext credentials for dozens of internal CISA systems starting in November 2025.
incidents.impact: Exposed AWS GovCloud keys and an RSA private key granting full read/write access to every CISA-IT GitHub repository, plus the ability to register rogue CI/CD runners. More than a week later many keys remained un-rotated. Senators and House Homeland Security leaders are demanding answers.

incidents.victim: GitHub (internal codebase); downstream: OpenAI, Grafana Labs, Mistral AI
incidents.vector: Attackers used credentials stolen in an earlier TanStack OIDC abuse wave to publish a malicious version (v18.95.0) of the Nx Console VS Code extension under a verified publisher; it was live for ~18 minutes. A GitHub employee endpoint auto-updated, exfiltrating secrets used to pivot into internal CI/CD.
incidents.impact: Approximately 3,800-4,000 internal GitHub repositories stolen. GitHub's CISO publicly named OpenAI, Grafana Labs, and Mistral AI as downstream victims. No customer-tenant data reported affected, but the breach demonstrates verified-publisher badges are not a safe install-time signal.

incidents.vector: Automated campaign pushed 5,718 malicious commits to 5,561 repos in a six-hour window on May 18, using forged author identities and a malicious GitHub Actions workflow ("SysDiag") plus a stealth "workflow-dispatch" backdoor that creates no visible CI runs until activated.
incidents.impact: Malicious workflows exfiltrated CI/CD secrets, cloud credentials, SSH keys, OIDC tokens, and source-code secrets to a C2 server. A week later ~83% of infected repos remained compromised; the Tiledesk open-source chatbot platform unknowingly propagated the malware to downstream users.

incidents.victim: Microsoft Azure durabletask Python SDK and @antv npm packages
incidents.vector: TeamPCP trojanized three versions (1.4.1-1.4.3) of Microsoft's officially-published durabletask Python SDK on PyPI during a ~35-minute window, and pushed 639 malicious package versions across 323 @antv npm packages (including echarts-for-react and size-sensor, ~1.1M-4.2M weekly downloads).
incidents.impact: Multi-stage payload steals npm tokens, GitHub PATs, and cloud credentials, and self-propagates by backdooring every package the victim can publish. Independent reporting characterized the durabletask second-stage payload as carrying a Linux disk wiper, raising destructive-impact potential alongside credential theft.

incidents.victim: Aerospace, defense, and telecom firms in US, Israel, UAE, and Middle East
incidents.vector: Targeted social engineering with personalized recruitment lures impersonating trusted hiring platforms; new "AppDomainManager hijacking" technique disables .NET application security mechanisms via legitimate config files to deploy six new RAT variants.
incidents.impact: Active espionage operations from mid-February through April 2026, timed to the Middle East regional conflict that began February 28. Six new RAT variants give the group multi-functional remote access for collection against high-value targets. Unit 42 assesses moderate-to-high confidence in attribution.

incidents.victim: Dozens of organizations across North America, Australia, and UK
incidents.vector: Voice phishing (vishing) calls to employees' personal phones, posing as IT/help desk demanding passkey or MFA enrollment, then routing victims to lookalike SSO portals to harvest credentials in real time and bypass MFA via adversary-in-the-middle relay.
incidents.impact: Attackers register a new MFA device for persistence, then use Python and PowerShell scripts to exfiltrate millions of files from SharePoint, OneDrive, Salesforce, and Zendesk. Extortion demands open in the millions and escalate via email spam, threatening voicemails to executives, and in severe cases swatting.

incidents.vector: SEO poisoning and AI chatbot recommendation poisoning surface fake download sites for legitimate utilities (CrystalDiskInfo, HWMonitor, FurMark, etc.). A ZIP archive sideloads a malicious DLL that silently deploys ScreenConnect remote-access software and a process-hollowing dropper into Microsoft-signed .NET binaries.
incidents.impact: Attackers selectively target high-end GPU systems for cryptocurrency mining and establish persistent remote access that could later support data theft, lateral movement, or ransomware. Microsoft has tracked 150+ malicious domains since March 2026. Notable for first observed AI-chatbot-driven malware delivery.

incidents.vector: Zero-day ViewState deserialization exploit (CVE-2026-5426) against KnowledgeDeliver, abusing hardcoded ASP.NET machine keys shipped identically across customer deployments before Feb 24, 2026.
incidents.impact: Mandiant responded to a compromised KnowledgeDeliver web server where attackers deployed the BLUEBEAM in-memory web shell, tampered with site JavaScript to show a fake "security plugin" prompt, and pushed Cobalt Strike Beacon payloads custom-encrypted for the victim organization.
